item.title: Ceuta troops absent as Spain holds National Day parade in Madrid
item.description: The parade took place against a tense political backdrop, after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for 29 November.

item.title: Portugal begins construction of high-speed rail line linking Lisbon and Porto
item.description: “Alongside the new Lisbon airport, high-speed rail lines represent the largest infrastructure projects the country will undertake this century," Miguel Pinto Luz, Portugal's minister of infrastructure and housing, said.

item.title: French navy intercepts and boards 'shadow fleet' ship, Macron says
item.description: Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence says the DF Peak tanker is involved in the transportation of Russian crude oil and that it is associated with the Sovcomflot shipping firm.

item.title: Citroën's iconic 2CV returns as an all-electric model
item.description: Almost 40 years after disappearing, the iconic 2CV returns at the Paris Motor Show as a fully electric city car, keeping things simple and affordable in an increasingly competitive market.

item.title: French investigators use DNA and vehicle tracking to solve stolen Renoirs case
item.description: The arrests were prompted by the "very strong suspicion that another heist was imminent," the Marseille prosecutor said.

item.title: Spain: National Day highlights territorial unity from Barcelona to Ceuta
item.description: Spain's National Day on Monday, 12 October, was marked by demonstrations in Barcelona in support of Spanish unity, while far-right leader Santiago Abascal visited Ceuta, the Spanish enclave on the North African coast.

item.title: Blindsided again by Trump, Europe puts on a brave face and rallies behind Ukraine
item.description: European leaders closed ranks and rallied behind Ukraine as news of the diesel deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin continued to send shockwaves across the alliance.

item.title: EU struggles to ramp up Red Sea mission as Houthis escalate attacks
item.description: The EU and Italy are pushing member states to bolster the Aspides naval mission in the Red Sea, but only two more warships have been pledged, exposing Europe’s thin defence capabilities as the Houthis threaten energy supply routes.

item.title: UK PM Burnham says 'status quo' with Brussels 'not good enough' as he details upcoming EU summit
item.description: Burnham has repeatedly signalled his intention to move the UK closer to the EU since taking office in July and recently said reentering the bloc was one of a number of options for the country moving forward.

item.title: EU-China trade deal raises fears Brussels will go soft on Beijing
item.description: The EU's new trade deal with China has eased fears of an escalating trade war, but it could also weaken the political momentum behind Brussels' plans to take a tougher stance against Beijing's economic practices.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 12th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 12th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EU agrees new security mission in Lebanon as UN peacekeepers prepare to leave
item.description: EU foreign ministers approved a civilian-military mission to train Lebanon’s armed forces. It will not replace UNIFIL, whose mandate ends in December. Personnel numbers and participating countries are yet to be confirmed.

item.title: NATO commander unveils strategy to make any attack on alliance ‘utterly futile’
item.description: Alexus Grynkewich says the new strategy aims to deny adversaries a foothold and dismantle their warfighting capabilities, telling the Warsaw Security Forum that NATO is prepared to block, blunt and break any attack.

item.title: 44-year-old woman rescued after 20 hours in sea, Greek coastguard says
item.description: The woman, from El Salvador, was found by the cargo ship MSC Rossella III, which was taking part in search efforts, the coastguard said in a statement.

item.title: Nuclear war and malicious use of AI could end humanity by 2100, scientists warn
item.description: They are among 17 global threats to human health according to a new study by The Lancet which aims to drive global action to address them.

item.title: Greece's social media ban for under-15s: What you need to know
item.description: The government argues that setting a clear age limit, combined with reliable age checks, will help protect children from potential risks associated with social media usage.

item.title: Hundreds of French supermarkets hit by cyberattack on refrigeration systems
item.description: Several supermarkets were forced to discard fresh and frozen food, Intermarché said, and have yet to estimate the losses. The Paris prosecutor has opened an investigation.

item.title: Paris’s oldest covered food market gutted by major overnight fire
item.description: Fire tore through Paris’s oldest covered food market in the Marais, leaving traders devastated. An investigation is under way and the market may stay shut for months.

item.title: Hard-right Reform party pledges to suspend UK asylum system for up to five years if elected
item.description: Reform has accused Labour of having "totally lost control" of the UK's borders, whilst Labour says small boat crossing figures have continued to come down in recent years.

item.title: Spreading the flow: cruise tourism helps Europe protect local identity
item.description: Europe’s tourism strategy is shifting to sustainable, year-round travel, promoting lesser-known destinations, local culture and smarter visitor management.

item.title: Explore the patterns of Qatar’s visual identity and architectural language
item.description: Cult explores the visual language of Qatar, where geometry isn’t ornamental. At the Doha Design District, we learn about 15 patterns from the Msheireb Pattern Collection, tracing their cultural and architectural origins, revealing how design can carry memory, identity and a sense of belonging.

item.title: Gijs de Best urges shared enforcement to curb illicit trade
item.description: Illicit trade costs governments billions and puts consumers at risk. Gijs de Best says only shared intelligence and enforceable rules can curb the problem.

item.title: Started planning summer 2027 holidays? Ryanair and easyJet announce 47 new flight routes
item.description: Ryanair has released its first 29 new flight routes for summer 2027, while easyJet has also confirmed 18 new routes from the UK.

item.title: Agios Efstratios: the first Greek island to get all its electricity from renewables
item.description: In ten months, the small island of Agios Efstratios has gone from relying entirely on fossil fuels to producing more than 90% of its electricity from renewable sources. Thanks to an EU-funded project, this volcanic island is now self-sufficient with green energy.

item.title: Ukraine passes minority rights law, paving way for breakthrough in EU accession talks
item.description: Ukraine’s parliament passed a minority rights law, easing a years-long dispute with Hungary. Diplomats expect Budapest to approve two more EU accession clusters on Tuesday, and Prime Minister Péter Magyar could meet President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Brussels on Thursday.

item.title: German firms outline new infrastructure and green energy plans in Baku
item.description: German industrial giants, including Siemens Energy, are exploring opportunities to support Azerbaijan's green energy transition, as the country aims to handle 30 million tonnes of transit cargo by 2030.

item.title: Did Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centres cause Russian bot activity to plummet?
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said social media had become less hostile following Kyiv's strikes on Russian technology giant Yandex's data centres, as web users report plummeting bot activity.

item.title: UAE calls for stronger Gulf defence as allies back Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attacks
item.description: Deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airport have brought fresh calls for joint Gulf defence, as Qatar warned the wider conflict was damaging global energy supplies.

item.title: Video shows major fire ravaging 400-year-old Paris food market
item.description: Footage shows the aftermath of a major overnight fire at Paris’s oldest covered food market, which dates back to 1615

item.title: What we know about Pope Leo XIV's upcoming operation to remove lung nodule
item.description: The Vatican press office has said doctors expect the pope's recovery to take around a week. That would make it possible for him to leave for his visit to Latin America as planned on 6 November.

item.title: What to know about Pope Leo XIV's upcoming lung surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is to undergo surgery this week to remove a lung nodule — a small growth of dense tissue inside the lung. Here is what to know about the procedure.

item.title: Miriam González launches new party to take on Spain’s big two in snap election
item.description: Lawyer Miriam González is entering politics with new party Democracia21. She is married to British politician Nick Clegg, former UK deputy prime minister, and says she wants to "regenerate Spanish politics".

item.title: Thales to open what could be Japan’s first foreign-run defence maintenance base
item.description: The facility could be the first in Japan set up by a foreign defence company to maintain military equipment and support its operation, according to Nikkei.

item.title: French MPs push exit tax on crypto above €800,000 and fines for undeclared wallets
item.description: French MPs want wealthy crypto investors who leave the country to pay tax on their paper gains, under an amendment backed in committee last week alongside fines of up to €10,000 for undeclared self-custody wallets, though every measure must be voted on again.

item.title: As drones reshape warfare, Lithuania brings them into the classroom
item.description: In Lithuania, children learn to build and programme drones at school. Similar projects exist in Germany. But what can pupils learn from these unmanned systems?

item.title: Citroën revives its classic 2CV with a new electric concept
item.description: Citroën has unveiled an all-electric concept inspired by its iconic 2CV, aiming to bring the classic model back to the road within the next two years. The compact vehicle combines retro styling with modern electric technology and is expected to start at around €15,000.

item.title: Headmaster and teacher shot at French school as 14-year-old teen arrested, police say
item.description: A third person was grazed in the shooting in the southern town of Aubagne, near Marseille, per police. Authorities said the headmaster and teacher were not in critical condition.

item.title: Americans Hall and Woodford win Nobel Prize in economics for stabilisation models
item.description: The economics prize is the only Nobel not among the original five created in the will of Swedish scientist Alfred Nobel, who died in 1896.

item.title: ‘Critical moment’: World leaders urged to course correct on nature protection ahead of COP17 summit
item.description: Game-changing global nature pact still has potential – but nations need to speed up progress, conservationists urge.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 12th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 12th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: You could own an entire Scottish island for €414,000 – but there’s a catch
item.description: Hildasay Island off the west coast of Shetland offers spectacular views and birdlife, but no real creature comforts.

item.title: ‘We still love you’: NATO envoy seeks to reassure Europe over US military pullback
item.description: US Ambassador to NATO, Matthew Whitaker, has enthused that there is no “love” lost between Washington and Brussels amid a more Europeanised NATO.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Russia ignored Trump's 'energy ceasefire' and kept attacking Ukraine
item.description: Zelenskyy addressed the Warsaw Security Forum in one of his first reactions to renewed turmoil with Washington, following Trump's surprise energy ceasefire announcement and controversial diesel deal with Russia.

item.title: IEA urges additional diesel releases ahead of key meeting
item.description: Tightening global diesel markets prompted the International Energy Agency to call on its members to accelerate previously agreed releases from strategic oil reserves, prioritising diesel. The IEA also asked member states to assess "whether additional diesel releases are necessary".

item.title: Chinese carmaker BYD considers opening a factory in France
item.description: France is among the European countries where BYD is considering opening a plant. According to vice-president Stella Li, "France is on the shortlist".

item.title: Independent Gibala beats Tusk’s party to win Krakow mayoral run-off
item.description: The new mayor took 62% of the vote in an election triggered after residents voted in May to oust his predecessor, and Łukasz Gibała warned that the city’s finances are in a disastrous state.

item.title: Cute cats and street fighters: The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week
item.description: Fontaines D.C. bring synths and psychedelia with their latest album 'Dopamine Chamber' while a new exhibition near Paris explores all things cute. Here's what to look out for this week.

item.title: EU leaders face budget showdown as Germany leads revolt over spending plans
item.description: An Irish compromise proposal for the EU’s long-term budget has drawn fire from the net-paying countries over its size and its focus on cutting ‘modern’ priorities. The Commission and MEPs have countered, warning of the risks of a less ambitious, more rigid budget.

item.title: What is ‘pilgra-merch’? The travel trend turning souvenirs into trip inspiration
item.description: Tourists are showing off how well-travelled they are through destination-specific grocery tote bags or branded hotel caps.

item.title: Fire totally destroys oldest covered food market in Paris, authorities say
item.description: The Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges in the Marais district has existed since 1615 and draws its name from the red outfits that orphans wore at a hospital near the market until 1772.
